reasons: Formula 1 applies a constant factor of 100 that does not appear in the Datadog source; the rules forbid applying unit scales in promql and require them to be proposed in notes only. Formula 2 has no such factor, so the two formulas are also internally inconsistent.

The unit scale is not justified: redis.cpu.time is a cumulative sum in seconds, so rate() gives a seconds-per-second value. Whether Datadog redis.cpu.sys is a percent or a ratio is not established in the request, so a scale proposal belongs in notes with a documentation link.
Template variable host has prefix host and default *, so both PromQL queries need a host=~"$host" matcher. Neither has one, so the candidate selects a different set of series.
Template variable key has prefix key and default *, so a key=~"$key" matcher is expected. The candidate omits it and does not mention the absence of a key label in notes.

The scope variable has no prefix and default *, so dropping it is correct. The metric and state=sys/user selection maps the quantity sensibly, and the translated outcome is appropriate because an OTel equivalent exists.
